items.t: "Thornhill" is both a City of Maple Ridge neighbourhood name and the board sub-area name (listed on the MLS as Thornhill MR, the form the guide page's feed cards carry). The City describes Thornhill as a heavily forested, mainly residential area with several farms and nurseries, with a large mountain-biking and hiking trail network on 256 Street. The City publishes no boundary for the neighbourhood or the MLS sub-area: Not verified as an official boundary.

Nearby areas: Albion to the southwest, Websters Corners to the southeast, Whonnock to the east, Ruskin further east, and the City of Mission across the eastern boundary. The guide feed's 249 Street cards show the page's scope overlapping Albion on that hillside.
There is no West Coast Express station in this sub-area.

Hazards and services: parcel-level ALR, floodplain, well and septic status and wildfire interface mapping for specific streets are not verified. Rural properties may be on wells and septic — wells are recorded in the provincial GWELLS database and onsite sewerage must comply with the Sewerage System Regulation, including the 30 m setback from a well unless professional advice is obtained.

blocks.text: Good to know about Thornhill Maple Ridge Guide

items.t: Thornhill's entire attached market is one street. Three townhome complexes — The Terraces, Terraces II and Rydge — all stand on 248 Street at the sub-area's southwest edge, in a sub-area otherwise made of forested acreage between 248 and 264 Streets; "Thornhill condos" and "Thornhill acreages" are effectively two different markets sharing one board name.
The developer and the board disagree about where Rydge is.

The same 249 Street property appears twice in the guide page's feed at the same price under two MLS numbers (once as Land, once as Residential), so the feed double-counts one parcel; and one feed card's header states an open house of 1:00–3:00 p.m. on November 1, 2026 while the same card's body text states 12:00–2:00 p.m. and then 1–3 p.m. — a one-hour conflict inside one card. No listing address or price beyond this conflict note is republished here.
Zero attached sales in a month with stock on the shelf.

The trail network is the area's signature amenity. The City counts 17 mountain-biking and hiking trails on 256 Street, moderately difficult, typically about an hour each, usable year-round — the 248 Street townhomes sit at the network's southwest corner, and Kanaka Creek Regional Park (Canyon Trail to Cliff Falls, Bell-Irving Hatchery) is at the west side. Guide-only details recorded as site copy only, not verified pass: the Thornhill Park and Hall details and the Thornhill Trails trailhead details quoted on the guide page.

A 500-acre industrial plan touches the north side. The North 256 Street Industrial Lands Area Plan covers both sides of 256 Street north of 128 Avenue — it changes long-term designations around those parcels without approving any construction, and it is a disclosure item for acreage listings in that pocket, not a development approval.
The Lougheed corridor position for this area.
Maple Ridge's OCP citation is unsettled in current sources. The guide page's census snapshot for Thornhill is likewise not verified — no Statistics Canada profile figure was opened for the sub-area.

No recreation centre, library branch or shopping centre sits inside this sub-area. The Maple Ridge Leisure Centre (11925 Haney Place), Maple Ridge Public Library (130 – 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road) and Town Centre shopping are all to the west; the serving hospital is Ridge Meadows Hospital, 11666 Laity Street, with the Urgent and Primary Care Centre at 121 – 11900 Haney Place, open 7 days a week, 9:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.

items.t: All of the attached stock sits at the southwest subdivision edge on 248 Street — The Terraces, Terraces II and Rydge — while the rest of the sub-area is freehold acreage.
No townhouse-complex card appears in the guide feed. The exact feed filter criteria beyond those labelled cards: Not verified.

No superlative is claimed: the detached ratio sits mid-pack among Maple Ridge's twelve sub-areas, and Thornhill is one of only two (with Silver Valley) where attached listings existed but recorded no sale.

Parks, recreation and transit: the City describes Thornhill's 256 Street trail network for mountain biking and hiking — 17 trails, moderately difficult, typically about an hour to complete, usable year-round; Kanaka Creek Regional Park (Metro Vancouver) sits at the west side, with the Canyon Trail to Cliff Falls and the Bell-Irving Hatchery; Whonnock Lake Park is in Whonnock to the east. No City recreation centre or library branch sits inside this sub-area; the Maple Ridge Leisure Centre, 11925 Haney Place, and the Maple Ridge Public Library (FVRL), 130 – 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road, are in the Town Centre to the west. There is no West Coast Express station in this sub-area.

blocks.text: Thornhill Maple Ridge Condos and Townhomes: streets and boundaries

items.t: Thornhill is the hillside area of Maple Ridge between Albion and Whonnock, and the City lists Thornhill among its named neighbourhoods on its neighbourhoods page.
The strata stock does not spread across the hill: all of it stands on 248 Street at the area's southwest edge, below the forested acreages that run east toward 264 Street.

blocks.text: Thornhill Maple Ridge Condos and Townhomes: the housing stock

items.t: Rydge, by Raicon Developments at 106 Avenue and 248 Street, is 61 three- and four-bedroom townhomes, the count stated on the developer's own presale record.

blocks.text: Thornhill Maple Ridge Condos and Townhomes: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Slope is the governing rule on Thornhill: the City's Natural Features Development Permit (NFDP) applies to any site with slopes of 15% or greater, and to sites within 50 metres (m) of a park boundary or floodplain boundary.

The City's sloping-sites bulletin requires a Geotechnical Letter of Assurance for development on a slope greater than 10%, and a full geotechnical report on or within 5 m of a slope greater than 20%; development is prohibited on slopes greater than 25% by the Zoning Bylaw.

Wildfire is the second overlay: the City's peer review of its Wildfire Hazard Development Permit Area records the proposed Thornhill polygon at over 580 hectares, with hazardous fuel types across the slope and critical telecommunications infrastructure on it, and puts construction in the area under National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) standards NFPA-1144 and NFPA-1141.

blocks.text: Thornhill Maple Ridge Condos and Townhomes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The City's 2026–2030 Capital Plan replaces the 248 Street drinking water pump station, with planning, design and construction commencing in 2028 — the station that serves the townhouse pocket's slope.
The same capital plan twins the supply main between 248 Street and the Albion Reservoir in 2027 and 2028 to support growth in the Albion and Thornhill service area.

SD42's Strategic Facilities Review expects Thornhill development to begin around 2030, as Albion and Silver Valley approach buildout — the planning fact behind the holding pattern on the acreages above the townhouses.
The forested slope above the complexes carries critical telecommunications infrastructure, which the City's wildfire peer review names as a reason the Thornhill polygon matters beyond its houses.

blocks.text: Thornhill Maple Ridge Condos and Townhomes: getting around

items.t: Route 746 is the bus service for the slope: Haney Place to Albion via 240 Street, 102 Avenue and Jackson Road, with some trips via Port Haney Station on the West Coast Express line.
The 746's routing puts the 248 Street complexes one street west of its 240 Street stops, so every transit trip from The Terraces or Rydge starts with the walk down 106 Avenue to 240 Street.

blocks.text: Thornhill Maple Ridge Condos and Townhomes: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the slope map before planning any addition: the NFDP checklist requires a colour-coded slope assessment of slopes over 15%, and the City does not support development where average natural slopes exceed 25%.
